mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for four consecutive weeks (-90.3 to -82.9). This momentum reflects an ongoing reopening trajectory that will continue mechanically into the next period absent a new shock, pushing the next 4-week mean above the last 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean is lower than its last 28-day mean despite the four-week rising streak, reject the momentum mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL time has fallen sharply (33.4 to 29.0). Once RESIDENTIAL drops below a 28-point threshold, it signals households are spending materially less time at home, which historically precedes a surge in discretionary retail and recreation trips within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 28.0 percentage points above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 33.4 to 29.0 over 3 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 2 weeks even after RESIDENTIAL crosses below the 28.0 threshold, or RETAIL_REC rises without RESIDENTIAL crossing it.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous acceleration in WORKPLACES (+11 pts over 3 weeks) and TRANSIT (+9.3 pts over 3 weeks) indicates coordinated policy-driven reopening of commuting infrastructure. When both series rise together, the combined restoration of commute-adjacent shopping and errand trips amplifies RETAIL_REC gains beyond what either series alone predicts, over a 4-week horizon.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -79.3 to -68.3 and TRANSIT rose from -83.4 to -74.1 over the same period
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week-ahead mean does not exceed its trailing 4-week mean despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continuing to rise jointly, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains deeply suppressed (-94.7) while TRANSIT is recovering faster (-74.1). When outdoor park access stays restricted relative to transit recovery, pent-up recreational demand redirects toward retail and recreation venues instead of parks, lifting RETAIL_REC over a 2-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: gap between TRANSIT and PARKS percent-change exceeds 15 points
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -74.1 vs PARKS at -94.7, a 20.6 point gap
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 2 weeks while the TRANSIT-PARKS gap remains above 15 points, reject this substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has rebounded rapidly (-68.0 to -53.0), approaching near-normal essential-trip behavior. Once GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -50, it signals that essential-trip caution has largely dissipated, which within one week typically spills over into renewed discretionary retail visits as the same households relax broader avoidance behavior.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -50.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at -53.0 in t-0w, up from -68.0 at t-3w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week following GROCERY_PHARM crossing -50.0, or increases without that crossing occurring, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-May seasonal warming independently drives outdoor and park-oriented leisure substitution; as PARKS activity has room to recover seasonally, some recreation demand that would otherwise flow to retail-and-recreation venues shifts to parks, dampening RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks relative to the recent uptrend.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2020-05-15, early reopening spring period
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean rises together with a rising PARKS series rather than being suppressed, the seasonal substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility plateaus (week-on-week change falls below 1.0 point) after weeks of decline, it signals that policy-driven relaxation has stalled, implying no further near-term loosening of retail access restrictions, which keeps RETAIL_REC flat or slightly lower over the following week.
candidate_trigger: week-on-week change in RESIDENTIAL falls below 1.0 point
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL weekly declines were -0.1, -2.3, -2.0 over the last three transitions
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues rising in the week after a RESIDENTIAL plateau (change <1.0 point), the policy-stall mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating WORKPLACES recovery combined with accelerating TRANSIT recovery over the last two weeks (both showing larger week-on-week gains than the prior two weeks) indicates a compounding commuting-and-errand recovery loop: more workplace trips generate more transit use, which in turn increases incidental retail stops, driving RETAIL_REC higher over a 4-week horizon.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES weekly gains accelerated from 0.6 to 5.4 points; TRANSIT weekly gains accelerated from 1.0 to 3.8 points
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next 4-week mean does not exceed the trailing 4-week mean despite accelerating joint gains in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, the compounding mechanism is rejected.
